scenes.title: 한 번의 공격 안에 있는 시간
lines: This is the training area in Monster Hunter Wilds. The hunter raises the great sword, strikes the dummy, then recovers. When you press the attack button, the character draws an arm back, strikes the opponent, then returns to a pose ready to move again. It may look like a single swing, but different parts of that time serve different purposes. Today, we will separate the lead-in, attack, and follow-through, including the standby pose that comes before them, and examine what information needs to be specified.

scenes.title: 한 번의 공격 안에 있는 시간
lines: In Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, watch Link change his leg position as he leaves the platform. Let us establish the starting point. The standby pose is the starting reference for the next action. Standing on the ground and being airborne call for different poses. From there, the character enters the lead-in, passes through impact, then moves into follow-through. Three moving stages and the standby pose make four elements.

scenes.title: 한 번의 공격 안에 있는 시간
lines: With those distinctions, we can state precisely which part we are changing.

scenes.title: 입력을 알아보게 하는 준비
lines: The first change from standby is the lead-in. The character may draw an arm back before swinging a sword, or lower the body before throwing a punch. This lets us anticipate the attack and its direction.

scenes.title: 입력을 알아보게 하는 준비
lines: Watch the instant the great sword rises over the hunter’s shoulder. There is still a gap between the blade and the target. Having a lead-in does not mean the movement must be slow. In fast action, right after the button press, a clear lead-in pose makes the response easier to feel. If the body goes through only a series of tiny changes, even when the input has already been processed, it can look as though nothing is happening.

scenes.title: 입력을 알아보게 하는 준비
lines: Within a short time, the body needs a shape clearly different from standby.

scenes.title: 입력을 알아보게 하는 준비
lines: The opponent can see this signal too. The attacker knows their input was accepted, while the opponent reads which action has begun. The lead-in provides information for both control and competition.

scenes.title: 타격 순간에 남는 자세
lines: When the hunter connects with the training dummy, a hit effect flashes at the contact point. After the lead-in, the attack enters the interval when it can hit. Hit detection checks the conditions for an attack to connect. The time when those checks are enabled is called the active interval. The checks are not necessarily active whenever the arm is moving.

scenes.title: 타격 순간에 남는 자세
lines: At the moment of impact, the attacker and the target may both briefly stop moving. This is called hit stop. A pose that would pass in an instant stays visible, so the direction of the hands, feet, and weapon matters. The lead-in pose signals the coming attack; the impact pose shows where its force was delivered.

scenes.title: 타격 뒤에도 공격은 이어진다
lines: Follow the tip of the hunter’s sword again. It continues moving after it passes the target. Even after landing a hit, the character does not immediately return to the starting pose. The swinging arm continues, the body absorbs the turn, and follow-through restores balance. This leaves a visible impression of what just happened.

scenes.title: 타격 뒤에도 공격은 이어진다
lines: At the same time, the game may briefly restrict the next action. If the opponent can exploit the opening after a powerful attack, choosing which attack to use becomes a decision. But what if the body is nearly back in standby while control is still locked? The attack looks finished, yet the next action will not happen. Over that same time, let the arm extend farther along the swing, and let the body absorb that force and regain its balance. The impression of the attack remains visible.

scenes.title: 타격 뒤에도 공격은 이어진다
lines: The time without control is used to express the motion.

scenes.title: 타격 뒤에도 공격은 이어진다
lines: It helps to distinguish visible follow-through from the recovery interval that restricts the next action. They are closely related, but need not end at the same moment. That difference determines how the next movement begins.

scenes.title: 동작의 끝과 조작의 재개
lines: First, imagine that follow-through must finish and the character must fully return to standby before another input is accepted. You must wait until the arm is withdrawn and the body straightens before you can run. Alternatively, running can be allowed during the return to standby. With no input, the original animation continues to its end. Press run, and running replaces the remaining return motion.

scenes.title: 동작의 끝과 조작의 재개
lines: A frame at which a transition to the next action is allowed is called a cancelable frame.

scenes.title: 동작의 끝과 조작의 재개
lines: A frame is one interval in a divided timeline. In our demonstration running at 60 frames per second, we will make the full clip 48 frames long and allow the next action from frame 36. The clip lasts 0.8 seconds, but control returns at 0.6 seconds. Compared with waiting for the full return, you can start running 0.2 seconds earlier. The finishing motion remains available on screen, while the next input can connect sooner.

scenes.title: 동작의 끝과 조작의 재개
lines: If animation length and the time until control returns are both described simply as action duration, different team members can easily understand different things.

scenes.title: 동작의 끝과 조작의 재개
lines: You also need to specify which actions are allowed next. Among running, jumping, and another attack, decide which become available at this point. Check whether the body looks ready to move as control returns. The animation brief can now specify both the final pose and the conditions for connecting to the next action.

scenes.title: 제작자가 공유할 네 기준
lines: We now have reference points for describing an attack. The starting standby pose, the attack pose where the force should read most clearly, the frame when hit detection becomes active, and the time until the next action is accepted. Fill the time from standby to attack with the lead-in, and use follow-through after the attack until the next action. With these reference points, the animator and the person building the game rules can discuss the same attack.

scenes.title: 제작자가 공유할 네 기준
lines: The four reference points provide a framework for the movement. The intended impression still needs more concrete direction. For example, even if the sword connects at the same moment, you can specify how far the shoulder turns, the height where the sword tip stops, and how forcefully the pose holds after the attack. Review and revise the timeline together with the pose references so that the numbers and expression form one coherent movement.

scenes.title: 제작자가 공유할 네 기준
lines: Let us watch the movement on the grid again. The transition from standby to lead-in makes the input visible. At impact, the force becomes visible. Follow-through carries the result of that force onward. Then, at the specified point, the next action can begin. A good attack animation goes beyond a single impressive pose: it makes all this information work together over time.
